sections.content:
6,540 people

were counted on the census as "senior police officers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Senior police officers co-ordinate the resources and activities of a specific geographical or functional area of generalised or specialised police work.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 45 to 49 years. Of the whole working population 11% were aged 45 to 49 years. For people working as "senior police officers", 28.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "senior police officers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 45 to 49 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "senior police officers" included:

  • head teachers and principals
  • information technology directors
  • senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "senior police officers" there were more men than women (73% compared with 27%).

This means "senior police officers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 73% and women made up 27% of "senior police officers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "senior police officers" included:

  • physical scientists
  • managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services
  • chief executives and senior officials

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "senior police officers", 7.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (98.3% compared with 1.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (99.4%) than self-employed (0.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
